change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Queries are interpolated here and again in runQuery, and three times on the shard path
findings.body:
`runSplitQuery` now calls `datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target. It then hands the result to `datasource.runQuery`, which calls `super.query()`. `DataSourceWithBackend.query` calls `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again for every target of the same datasource (`packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185`). `applyTemplateVariables` is not idempotent (`datasource.ts:1110-1141`). It re-runs `templateSrv.replace` on the already-interpolated expr, step and legendFormat, and it calls `addAdHocFilters(expr, adhocFilters)` again (`datasource.ts:1127`).

Ad hoc filters that are added after a parser or label filter are likely to be appended twice. I read `addLabelToQuery` (`modifyQuery.ts:147-209`). Only the stream-selector branch de-duplicates (`labelExists`, `modifyQuery.ts:494`). I did not trace the label-filter branch to confirm it lacks a check. A value that contains `$` after the first pass, for example a variable value or an escaped regex, would also be interpolated a second time.

On the shard path, `runShardSplitQuery` interpolates, then `splitQueriesByStreamShard` calls `runSplitQuery` (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:163`), which interpolates again, then `runQuery` interpolates a third time. Before this change the shard path interpolated without ad hoc filters (`interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars)`). The split path passed raw targets, so interpolation happened once, in `runQuery`.

The new tests mock `datasource.runQuery`. They therefore cannot see the interpolation that `super.query` performs. Either drop the interpolation from one layer, or add a test through the real `query()` path with ad hoc filters and a parser. The test should assert that the filter appears once.

findings.title: Assertion of 5 applyTemplateVariables calls hard-codes the double interpolation
findings.body: `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` counts one call from `runShardSplitQuery` plus four calls from the nested `runSplitQuery`, one per shard request. The number is therefore coupled to the shard group count and to the redundant re-interpolation described on `querySplitting.ts:299`. If the duplication is removed, or the shard mock data changes, the test breaks without any behavioural change. Assert the interpolated expr that reaches `runQuery` instead of the call count. The mock replacements at lines 56-58 and 173-175 also mutate the incoming `query` in place, which hides whether the real function returns a new object.

findings.title: New test mocks runQuery, so it does not cover the real interpolation path
findings.body: The test stubs `datasource.runQuery`. It only proves that `runSplitQuery` interpolates. It does not prove that the final request is interpolated correctly or exactly once. It also uses `replace` and `getVariables` mocks that replace `$__auto`, whereas the real `applyTemplateVariables` strips `__auto` and `__range` from `scopedVars` so the backend can interpolate them (`datasource.ts:1113`). Interpolating `$__auto` in the frontend before the split may therefore differ from production, where `templateSrv` may handle `$__auto` differently. A test with ad hoc filters would also be useful.

contracts.action: runSplitQuery now applies datasource.applyTemplateVariables to each target before splitting
contracts.equivalent_path: DataSourceWithBackend.query applies applyTemplateVariables per target when runQuery executes (called through super.query)
contracts.before_after: Before: targets reached runQuery raw and were interpolated once in super.query. After: they are interpolated in runSplitQuery and again in super.query, and the interpolation is not idempotent (ad hoc filters are re-added).
contracts.visible_effect: Possible duplicated ad hoc filter clauses or double-processed variable values in the executed LogQL when ad hoc filters are present.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong or odd query; no error is raised.

contracts.action: runShardSplitQuery replaces interpolateVariablesInQueries with applyTemplateVariables including request.filters
contracts.equivalent_path: datasource.query / runLiveQueryThroughBackend call applyTemplateVariables once with request.filters (datasource.ts:324, 377)
contracts.before_after: Before: interpolation without ad hoc filters, then runSplitQuery and runQuery. After: interpolation with filters, then nested runSplitQuery interpolation, then runQuery interpolation, so three passes.
contracts.visible_effect: Same as above, on the sharded query path.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent; the extra passes run for every shard request.

summary: The change runs `applyTemplateVariables` (with ad hoc filters) inside `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery`. `runQuery` then runs it again through `DataSourceWithBackend.query`. The shard path now interpolates three times, because `runSplitQuery` is nested inside `runShardSplitQuery`. The function is not idempotent, so ad hoc filters and `$`-containing values can be processed twice. I did not trace the label-filter branch of `addLabelToQuery`, so whether filters are actually appended twice after a parser is unconfirmed. The new tests mock `runQuery` and cannot detect this. The `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` assertion also bakes in the redundancy.
